Yes, demand was too high on 16 June 2025.

**Peak demand:** 1324.4 kW at 08:15, which is 6% above the 1250 kW contract limit [data: get_demand].

**Over-contract intervals:** Two 15-minute intervals exceeded the contract [data: get_demand]:
- 08:00 → 1307.1 kW
- 08:15 → 1324.4 kW (peak)

This is the "Monday morning simultaneous start" scenario (S2), where the morning startup surge pushed demand just above the contract limit for about half an hour [data: get_plant_overview].

I have the answer from the plant documents.

Per **SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown**, reflow ovens must be switched **OFF, not left in standby**, because an oven in standby draws **36% of its 70 kW rating = 25.2 kW** for as long as it stays on — a large idle load that produces nothing. A properly switched-off oven uses only about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]. This is also reinforced in the **EQ-01 Reflow Oven Manual**, which states standby at 36% (25.2 kW per oven) is still a large load and should be avoided unless boards are inside [source: docs/knowledge/equipment/EQ-01_reflow_oven.md#EQ-01 Reflow Oven Manual > Energy-saving notes].

**Incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20):** RF-02 was left in standby all weekend. Weekend energy was about **1,556 kWh** versus about **346 kWh** normal, an excess of about **1,210 kWh** from that single oven [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

answer:
According to the demand-exceedance procedure:

**Shed first:** EV charging (EV-01) is the first load to be paused — it's listed as Order 1 in the load-shed playbook because it has no effect on production. [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]

**Loads that must never be shed:**
- Server room (DC-01) — a continuous critical load, never part of any load-shed action [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]
- Running molders mid-cycle (IM-01 to IM-04) [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]
- Reflow ovens with boards inside (RF-01 to RF-03) [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]
